> 大畜。利貞。不家食，吉。利涉大川。

Hexagram 26 is the large version of storage, and the character's construction needs a caution before anything else.

## 畜, and what the dictionary actually says

說文: 畜，田畜也。《淮南子》曰：玄田為畜.

Xu Shen builds the character from 玄 and 田, and says outright that he is quoting the 淮南子. That is a Han-dynasty account, and bronze and oracle-bone scholarship has other explanations, none of which has won.

So it can be told, and it cannot be asserted as the oracle-bone original.

The extension is 畜養, to keep and to store. In the classics 畜 and 蓄 are interchangeable — 經典釋文: 大畜，本又作蓄.

So the name is read xù, nourishing, not chù, livestock. 大畜 is 大蓄: great storage.

## 輹 is not 輻

九二 輿說輹.

說文: 輹，車軸縛也 — the binding between the carriage box and the axle. The old name for it is 伏兔, the crouching rabbit.

This is the character the book has to separate from 輻.

輻 are the spokes from rim to hub — the character used in 小畜's 輿說輻.
輹 is the wooden binding of the box to the axle — the character used here.

Two characters, close in shape, different in meaning, and the received text does not have them mixed up. They are two pictures.

And 脫輹 already existed as a phrase before the 易: 左傳·僖公十五年, 車說其輹，火焚其旗 — same action, a carriage coming apart from its axle.

Lose the 輹 and the box separates from the axle: the cart cannot move. Which is why the line is a stop, and why 大畜 opens with stopping.

## 曰閑輿衛

九三 良馬逐，利艱貞；曰閑輿衛，利有攸往.

曰 here is a particle with no meaning — Wang Yinzhi's 經傳釋詞 makes the point. It is not "he said."

閑: to practise, to drill. 輿衛: carriage and guard, the equipment of movement.

So: drill the carriage and the guard, store the capability, and then it is beneficial to go.

## 童牛之牿 / 豶豕之牙

牿 has two readings: the crossbar fixed on a young ox's horns (the 周禮's 楅衡), or a pen for cattle (說文 牿，牛馬牢也).

This book takes the crossbar: fit the bar while the horns are not yet grown, and stop the goring before it exists.

豶 is a castrated boar. 牙 has two readings: the boar's tusks, or the wooden post it is tethered to (通 枒).

This book takes the tusks: quiet the animal's inward drive, and the tusks are there but do not wound. Not pulling the teeth out — settling the temper.

Both lines are the same idea at two scales: the correction is applied before the capacity to injure has formed. Which is the classic 未發 — before it arises — and it is the only place in the six lines where the verdict is 元吉.

## 何天之衢

Top line: 何天之衢，亨.

何 is 荷, to carry on the shoulder. 衢 is the great road, open on all four sides.

Carrying the open road of heaven: storage at its limit has become passage with nothing blocking it.

Which completes the hexagram's curve: 大畜 begins by stopping the cart, and ends by carrying a road. The stored thing was never the object — it was the ability to move once the stopping was over.

## 多識前言往行，以畜其德

The 象: know widely the words and deeds of former ages, and thereby store one's virtue.

The object of storage is made explicit, and it is not goods. It is recorded conduct.

Which is a very unusual instruction for a hexagram named after accumulation: the thing worth holding is other people's precedent, and the reason is that it is the only material that does not have to be manufactured again.

## The test

Take a stock you are building — savings, credentials, inventory. Ask which of the two words describes it: 蓄 (feeding a capacity) or 積 (piling a quantity). The hexagram's 畜 is the first, and its sign is that the stored thing can be deployed as a road.
